{"id": "7c1dadc1-96da-4b51-a044-4a3bf407b356", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_rqUr9a1FDKssrdAWsnucJx", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Managing Skills from Chat\\\\n\\\\n## Skill Type Glossary\\\\n\\\\n| Type | Display Name | Description | Managed by |\\\\n|------|-------------|-------------|------------|\\\\n| **SYSTEM** | *(hidden)* | Built-in skills shipped with the agent (e.g. investigations, recommendations). Never visible to users. | Engineering team |\\\\n| **LEARNED** | Managed skills | Skills created by DevOps Agent. Editable and refreshed from Chat. | DevOps Agent / User (via Chat edits + refresh) |\\\\n| **USER** | Custom skills | Skills created and updated by the user through chat. Full CRUD operations supported. | User (via these tools) |\\\\n\\\\nSome managed skills can be refreshed through their dedicated tools.\\\\n\\\\n## Managed Skills Are Becoming Memories\\\\n\\\\nManaged (LEARNED) skills are migrating to memory stores: the same learned content, held as\\\\nmemories instead of a skill. The migration runs per agent space, so at any moment a given\\\\nkind may exist as a skill, as a memory store, or both during the transition.\\\\n\\\\n**When both exist for the same kind, the memory store is the home and the LEARNED skill is the\\\\nstale copy.** Read and edit the memory, not the skill, and tell the user where it now lives.\\\\n\\\\n1. When a request concerns learned understanding the DevOps Agent generates (the learned\\\\n   stores that the `manage-memories` skill\\'s glossary enumerates), check for a memory store of\\\\n   that name before reaching for `get_skill`.\\\\n2. If a memory store exists for it, load the `manage-memories` capability and work there,\\\\n   following its learned-store workflow.\\\\n3. If only the skill exists, this space has not migrated yet \\\\u2014 use the skill tools as below.\\\\n4. Do not \\\\\"fix\\\\\" a migrated skill by editing the leftover skill copy; that edit does not reach\\\\n   the agents now reading the memory.\\\\n\\\\n## Hard Rules\\\\n\\\\n- Create and delete apply only to custom (USER) skills \\\\u2014 managed (LEARNED) skills cannot be created or deleted from Chat.\\\\n- To edit a managed skill\\'s content, use `update_skill`. Do not silently substitute a custom skill that happens to share a name \\\\u2014 confirm you are editing the intended skill.\\\\n- Editing a managed (LEARNED) skill has refresh/durability considerations \\\\u2014 see \\\\\"Edit a Managed Skill\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n## General\\\\n\\\\nWhen the user refers to a skill by name and you don\\'t have its knowledge_item_id, call `list_skills` to find it by name and confirm with the user before proceeding.\\\\n\\\\n## Operations\\\\n\\\\n### Create a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to create a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Check for existing skills first** \\\\u2014 call `list_skills` and review the results. If an existing skill covers a similar domain or purpose, suggest updating it instead of creating a new one. For example, if the user asks to \\\\\"create a skill for RDS troubleshooting\\\\\" and there\\'s already an \\\\\"investigate-rds-issues\\\\\" skill, propose adding the new instructions to that skill. Only proceed with creation if no existing skill is a good fit, or the user explicitly wants a new one.\\\\n2. **Gather requirements** \\\\u2014 purpose, instructions, and whether the skill needs reference files\\\\n   - A skill only needs SKILL.md if the instructions fit in one document\\\\n   - Add reference files when the skill needs: runbook templates, API reference docs, configuration examples, troubleshooting decision trees, or service-specific guides that would bloat SKILL.md\\\\n   - Organize reference files by purpose: `references/` for documentation, `assets/` for templates and config files\\\\n   - Keep SKILL.md focused on the workflow and decision logic; put detailed reference material in separate files that the agent loads on demand\\\\n2. **Generate SKILL.md** with valid YAML frontmatter and markdown body\\\\n3. **Call `create_skill`** with title, content, and optionally resources\\\\n   - `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\")`\\\\n   - If the skill needs reference files: `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\", resources={\\\\\"references/guide.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Guide content\\\\\", \\\\\"references/examples.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Examples\\\\\"})`\\\\n4. **Show the user what was created** \\\\u2014 mention the skill name, description, and key steps. Do not show the ID.\\\\n5. **Ask the user to confirm** \\\\u2014 Use `ask_user` to confirm activation:\\\\n   ```\\\\n   ask_user(\\\\n     question=\\\\\"Would you like me to activate this skill?\\\\\",\\\\n     options=[\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Activate\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Make this skill available for use\\\\\"},\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Keep inactive\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Save the skill but don\\'t activate it yet\\\\\"}\\\\n     ]\\\\n   )\\\\n   ```\\\\n6. **On confirmation** \\\\u2014 call `activate_skill` with the knowledge_item_id to make it live\\\\n7. **The skill is now available** \\\\u2014 `create_skill` returns the skill content in its response, so you already have the instructions. No need to call `get_skill` separately. Close the flow in prose (e.g. \\\\\"Skill is now active.\\\\\"). Do not call `ask_user` again after activation \\\\u2014 no follow-up menus.\\\\n\\\\n### Update a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to edit or update a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Read current content** \\\\u2014 use `get_skill` to get the current SKILL.md content\\\\n2. **Apply changes** \\\\u2014 modify the content as requested\\\\n3. **Call `update_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id and updated content\\\\n   - `update_skill(knowledge_item_id=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\")`\\\\n   - To add a resource file: `update_skill(knowledge_item_id=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\", resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/new.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"ADD\\\\\", \\\\\"file_content\\\\\": \\\\\"# New content\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - To edit a resource file: `update_skill(..., resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/guide.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"EDIT\\\\\", \\\\\"file_content\\\\\": \\\\\"# Updated content\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - To delete a resource file: `update_skill(..., resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/old.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"DELETE\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - Multiple mutations can be combined in a single call\\\\n\\\\n### Edit a Managed Skill (LEARNED)\\\\n\\\\nManaged skills hold learned content, so a direct edit follows the **same durability rule as a learned memory store**: it is **transient** \\\\u2014 the DevOps Agent\\'s next regeneration overwrites it. Confirm this kind has not already migrated to a memory store (see \\\\\"Managed Skills Are Becoming Memories\\\\\" above for that routing) before editing here, then apply the skill-specific mechanics below and tell the user a direct edit may not persist.\\\\n\\\\nSkill-specific mechanics for the direct edit:\\\\n1. **Confirm the target** \\\\u2014 read `skillKnowledgeItemId` from the page context.\\\\n2. **Make the edit** \\\\u2014 call `get_skill` for current content, then `update_skill`.\\\\n\\\\n### Delete a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to remove a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Identify the skill** \\\\u2014 use `list_skills` if needed\\\\n2. **Confirm** \\\\u2014 always ask the user to confirm before deleting\\\\n3. **Call `delete_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id\\\\n4. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm deletion\\\\n\\\\n### Read a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to see a skill\\'s content, explain what a skill does, or view its files:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `get_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id to get the SKILL.md content\\\\n2. **Explain** \\\\u2014 summarize the skill\\'s purpose, steps, and when it\\'s used\\\\n3. **If the skill has resource files** \\\\u2014 call `get_skill` with `return_manifest=true` to see all files, then use `path` to read specific resource files\\\\n\\\\n### List Skills\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to see their skills:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `list_skills`** \\\\u2014 returns agent space skills\\\\n2. **Present every skill individually** \\\\u2014 list each skill as a bullet: name \\\\u2014 description. Never group, merge, or deduplicate skills.\\\\n\\\\n### Enable or Disable a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to enable, disable, activate, or deactivate a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `toggle_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id and `enabled=true` or `enabled=false`\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new status. Disabled skills remain in the agent space but are not loaded by agents\\\\n\\\\n### Change Agent Type\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to change which agent types can use a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `update_skill_agent_type`** with the knowledge_item_id and the desired agent_types list \\\\u2014 see the tool\\'s `agent_types` parameter for the accepted values\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new agent type targeting\\\\n\\\\n## SKILL.md Format\\\\n\\\\nCreate a valid SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and markdown body:\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: my-skill-name\\\\ndescription: Brief description of what this skill does. Be specific about when\\\\n  the agent should use this skill (minimum 100 characters recommended).\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Skill Title\\\\n\\\\nInstructions for the agent when this skill is activated.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n- Condition 1\\\\n- Condition 2\\\\n\\\\n## Steps\\\\n1. Step one\\\\n2. Step two\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Frontmatter Rules\\\\n- `name`: Required. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (max 64 chars). Must not start or end with a hyphen. Example: `rds-throttling-investigation`\\\\n- `description`: Required. Brief explanation of when to use this skill (min 100 chars recommended, max 1024 chars).\\\\n\\\\n### Resource Files\\\\n\\\\nSkills can include reference files alongside SKILL.md. Reference files provide additional context the agent can load on demand. Use resource files when the skill needs supporting documentation, examples, API references, or other supplementary content.\\\\n\\\\n**Allowed file types:** `.md`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.xml`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.webp`, `.pdf`\\\\n\\\\n**Restrictions:**\\\\n- No script files (`.sh`, `.py`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.rb`, `.pl`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.exe`)\\\\n- No `scripts/` directory\\\\n- No files with shebang (`#!`) content\\\\n- Maximum 100 files, 6 MB total\\\\n\\\\n## Example\\\\n\\\\nUser: \\\\\"Create a skill that helps investigate Lambda cold start issues\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n1. Generate SKILL.md:\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: investigate-lambda-cold-starts\\\\ndescription: Investigate Lambda cold start latency issues by analyzing CloudWatch\\\\n  metrics, X-Ray traces, and function configuration. Use when users report slow\\\\n  Lambda response times or CloudWatch shows elevated Init Duration metrics.\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Investigating Lambda Cold Starts\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n- User reports slow Lambda response times\\\\n- CloudWatch shows elevated Duration or Init Duration metrics\\\\n\\\\n## Steps\\\\n1. Check the function\\'s **Init Duration** metric in CloudWatch for the last 24h\\\\n2. Look at **Provisioned Concurrency** settings \\\\u2014 if not configured, cold starts are expected\\\\n3. Check the function\\'s **memory size** \\\\u2014 larger memory = faster init\\\\n4. Review X-Ray traces for init segment duration breakdown\\\\n5. Check if the function uses VPC \\\\u2014 VPC-attached Lambdas have longer cold starts\\\\n6. For detailed remediation options, read `references/remediation-guide.md`\\\\n7. Recommend: enable Provisioned Concurrency, increase memory, or use SnapStart (Java)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n2. If the skill needs reference files:\\\\n```python\\\\ncreate_skill(\\\\n    title=\\\\\"Investigate Lambda Cold Starts\\\\\",\\\\n    content=<SKILL.md above>,\\\\n    resources={\\\\n        \\\\\"references/remediation-guide.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Cold Start Remediation\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Provisioned Concurrency\\\\\\\\n...\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\"references/metrics-reference.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Key CloudWatch Metrics\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Metric | Description |\\\\\\\\n...\\\\\"\\\\n    }\\\\n)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n3. Otherwise: `create_skill(title=\\\\\"Investigate Lambda Cold Starts\\\\\", content=<SKILL.md above>)`\\\\n4. Use `ask_user` to confirm activation:\\\\n   ```\\\\n   ask_user(\\\\n     question=\\\\\"I\\'ve created the skill in inactive state.
